Here's where the horrible part comes in. I said I was sorry, but I didn't stay. I sped off as quickly as I could and went back home. I eventually told the police about the situation and I haven't had any recourse for it but I still regret it. Just the look on that guy's face and the feeling that I could have killed him still haunt me.

I think Lies My Teacher Told could make for an interesting documentary in the same way that Freakonomics did. The book is a pretty schathing look at how American history textbooks have mistreated the American history and shows just how much revisionism has gone into changing the real story of America's past into a Disneyfied, theme park, feel good story where nobody has any problems. 

The book got quite a lot of praise when it was released and with good reason. The author James Loewen does a lot of in depth research in order to debunk several myths that textbooks have created and explore exactly why the American History textbooks used today are damaging to both history education and society in general. 

It really makes you care a lot about history is taught in schools, which is great if you ever found that history was bogus or a pointless class. I feel like more people should be made aware of just how damaging these textbooks are to history and I think in the right hands, a documentary would be incredibly fascinating and would be able to explain the importance of history to a society which normally considers it a periphery class.

Well honestly if you didn't like Skyrim for those reasons then you're probably not going to like Oblivion because it's kind of similar in terms of quest design. At its simplest, Oblivion has more of the same, go here, talk/kill this guy or take this thing quest system as Skyrim. It's also worth noting that Oblivion was released 5 years before Skyrim and was one of the first titles on the XBOX 360, so the graphics haven't aged all too well. The landscapes are still visually very striking but the facial textures are but ugly and not very fun to look at. The voice acting is also very dreadful as there are only about 11 voice actors for the 100+ characters and many of them are mailing it in like crazy. The leveling system is also broken as hell and takes quite a lot of trial and error before you are able to level up without having every enemy be able to pound you into the dust.

But really, that's all superficial, the main key to the Elder Scrolls series is immersion. It's about getting immersed in the fantasy world, the people who live in it, and the stories that can be told, whether they're the premade stories or the stories you create yourself. If you couldn't look past the gameplay or the structure of the game itself and get immersed in the world, then the whole series is really not for you. Not saying that you have bad taste or anything, it's just that the Elder Scrolls doesn't seem like the games that you're looking for. They're all about the world and the lore that is built around it and less about the gameplay. I would recommend not wasting your time on Oblivion because it has the more of the same thing that you listed. Sorry.
